articles.full_text:
NEW DELHI: The IMD has forecast
rain, thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds across several parts of the states while Delhi and neighbouring areas may experience thunderstorms and winds reaching 50 kmph, parts of southern India are likely to see gusty winds reaching 60 kmph. Heatwave conditions are also expected to persist in isolated parts of Maharashtra’s coastal belt.
Delhi weather tomorrow
The IMD has forecast rainfall in several parts of Delhi on Sunday, along with thunderstorms, lightning and strong winds reaching speeds of up to 50 kmph in some areas.
According to the weather department, a western disturbance its neighbouring areas, along with an upper-air cyclonic circulation over Haryana and adjoining northwestern Uttar Pradesh, is likely to influence weather conditions in Delhi and nearby states.
West Bengal weather tomorrow
Parts of south Bengal, including Kolkata, may experience rain during the initial days of the five-day Durga Puja festival. The IMD has forecast light to moderate rainfall at a few places from October 15 to 17, with Shashthi, the opening day of the festival, falling on October 17.
Light rain or thundershowers are likely at one or two places in south Bengal on Saptami and Ashtami, October 18 and 19, respectively.
Mainly dry weather is expected across south Bengal on Navami and Dashami, October 20 and 21.
Maharashtra weather tomorrow
The IMD has issued a heatwave warning for the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) and Maharashtra’s coastal Konkan belt until October 12.
Heatwave conditions are likely at isolated places in districts of south Konkan, while hot and humid conditions may prevail at isolated places in north Konkan, according to the IMD’s Regional Meteorological Centre.
The weather is expected to normalise on Sunday, October 11, and Monday, October 12, with green warnings, indicating that no adverse weather action is required, returning across Maharashtra.
Maximum temperatures are likely to rise gradually by 2-3 degrees Celsius in some parts of the state over the next 48 hours, followed by a further increase of 1-3 degrees Celsius. Maximum temperatures are expected to remain between 37 and 39 degrees Celsius in parts of interior Maharashtra on October 10.
The Mumbai Metropolitan Region is an urban agglomeration spread across nine municipal corporations in Mumbai and the adjoining districts of Thane, Palghar and Raigad.
Jharkhand weather tomorrow
The southwest monsoon is likely to withdraw from Jharkhand over the next four days, as the state has recorded a rainfall deficit of 2%, according to the IMD.
The monsoon has already withdrawn from northwestern districts and parts of central Jharkhand, including Garhwa, Chatra, Palamu, Latehar, Lohardaga, Ranchi, Hazaribagh and Koderma.
Uttar Pradesh weather tomorrow
West Uttar Pradesh may receive showers on Sunday, October 11. Rainfall activity is expected to continue in parts of the state over the weekend, although the latest forecast does not specify a heavy rainfall warning for Uttar Pradesh during this period.
Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Rajasthan weather
Uttarakhand is likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall between October 11 and 14. Gusty winds reaching 30-40 kmph, with gusts up to 50 kmph, are also expected.
Himachal Pradesh may experience isolated to scattered rainfall on October 13 and 14.
West Rajasthan is likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall on October 11 and 12, while east Rajasthan may see showers on October 12. Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds are also forecast in parts of west Rajasthan on Sunday.
Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh are likely to experience fairly widespread to widespread rainfall on Saturday, accompanied by isolated thunderstorms and lightning.
Northeast weather forecast
Assam and Meghalaya may experience rainfall on October 11, with another spell expected on October 13 and 14.
Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura are likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall between October 11 and 14. Thunderstorms and lightning are also forecast over parts of the Northeast.
Central India weather forecast
East Madhya Pradesh is likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall, with showers expected to continue until October 11. Chhattisgarh may also experience isolated to scattered rainfall.
Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 30-40 kmph, with gusts up to 50 kmph, are likely over east Madhya Pradesh on Sunday.
South India weather forecast
Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall between October 11 and 14. Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph, with gusts up to 60 kmph, are likely through October 12.
Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema may experience isolated to scattered rainfall over the coming days. Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph, with gusts up to 60 kmph, are likely over these regions. Strong surface winds are also forecast.
South interior Karnataka is likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall, while isolated heavy rain, thunderstorms and lightning are expected on Friday. Coastal Karnataka may also experience isolated to scattered showers through October 14.
Lakshadweep is likely to receive fairly widespread to widespread rainfall, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph, with gusts up to 60 kmph.
Other regions
Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim may experience fairly widespread to widespread showers followed by isolated to scattered rainfall on October 11.
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are likely to receive fairly widespread to widespread rainfall on October 11.
IMD’s latest forecast for the next few days
The IMD has forecast continued rainfall and thunderstorms across several regions over the coming days, with gusty winds likely in parts of northern, central and southern India. Meanwhile, the southwest monsoon is expected to withdraw from Jharkhand over the next four days, having already retreated from several northwestern and central districts of the state.

Weather Update: IMD issues yellow alert for thunderstorms in Kerala, Tamil Nadu; rain likely in several states
The IMD issued a yellow alert for thunderstorms, lightning, and gusty winds in Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Lakshadweep, while rain is likely across several states. Hot and humid conditions are also expected in parts of Coastal Karnataka, Konkan, and Goa.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a yellow alert for thunderstorm, lightning and gusty winds for several regions including Lakshadweep, Kerala and Tamil Nadu. The weather department has also warned of hot and humid weather at isolated places over Coastal Karnataka, Konkan and Goa.
Rainfall is likely across several parts of India on Sunday including Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Odisha and Jharkhand, among others. The Andaman and Nicobar Islands may also experience widespread rainfall, while parts of southern India, including Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Lakshadweep, are likely to receive showers.
The IMD has also forecast strong surface winds at isolated places across Andhra Pradesh on Sunday.
Yellow alert for thunderstorm
According to the IMD, thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds of 40-50 kmph are likely at isolated places in Kerala, Mahe, Lakshadweep, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal. Similar conditions, with wind speeds of 30-40 kmph, are expected in parts of Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha and West Rajasthan.
Isolated thunderstorms accompanied by lightning are also likely in Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura. Strong surface winds are expected at isolated places in Andhra Pradesh.
Rain and thunderstorms in southern India
Kerala, Mahe, Lakshadweep, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are likely to experience thunderstorms and gusty winds. The IMD has also forecast rainfall across parts of the southern peninsula, with Kerala and Mahe likely to receive rain between October 11 and 14.
Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema may experience gusty winds, while parts of Karnataka are expected to see rainfall and thunderstorms in the coming days.
Weather conditions in eastern and northeastern India
Rainfall is likely across the Andaman and Nicobar Islands on October 11, with isolated to scattered showers expected from October 12 to 16. In eastern India, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim may receive rain on October 11 and again on October 16, while Gangetic West Bengal is likely to see rainfall between October 14 and 16.
Jharkhand may experience rain from October 11 to 13, Bihar on October 11 and again on October 15 and 16, and Odisha between October 11 and 16. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are also likely in Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim in the coming days.
Meanwhile, Arunachal Pradesh may receive isolated to scattered rainfall on October 11 and again on October 15 and 16. Assam and Meghalaya are likely to experience showers on October 11 and between October 13 and 16, while Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura may receive rainfall from October 11 to 16.
Northwest and Central India weather
Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh and adjoining areas are likely to receive widespread rainfall on October 13 and 16, with isolated to scattered showers expected on October 11 and between October 14 and 15. Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand may also experience rainfall during this period. Haryana, West Uttar Pradesh, Chandigarh, Delhi and Punjab are likely to receive scattered showers over the coming days. West Rajasthan is likely to experience rain on October 11 and 16.
In Central India, West Madhya Pradesh is likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall on October 11 and 12, while Chhattisgarh may experience showers between October 12 and 16.
Hot and humid weather likely in coastal regions
Apart from rain and thunderstorms, hot and humid weather is likely at isolated places over Coastal Karnataka, Konkan and Goa on October 11.
